---
doc_id: D09
title: Sunita Rao v. State Insurance Corporation
court: SC
year: 2001
bench_size: 2
aliases: (2001) 3 SCC 77
---
[None] IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA (FICTIONAL DEMO). Civil Appeal No. 66 of 2000.
[Facts] The insured's claim under a fire policy was repudiated on the ground that intimation was given after the period stipulated in the policy.
[Issue] Whether delay in intimation of loss, by itself, defeats a genuine insurance claim.
[Reasoning] A condition requiring prompt intimation is intended to enable the insurer to investigate. Where the insurer has in fact investigated and the claim is otherwise genuine, delay alone is not a ground for repudiation. The insurer's surveyor confirmed the loss.
[Decision] The appeal is allowed and the insurer shall settle the claim.
